name: Tirzepatide

b.x: 20.2% body weight gone at 72 weeks, and that was the average, not the ceiling. Tirzepatide (LY3298176, CAS 2023788-19-2) is a 39-amino acid acylated lipopeptide sold as Zepbound for obesity and Mounjaro for type 2 diabetes. It activates both glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptors simultaneously. The dual receptor mechanism separates tirzepatide from single-target GLP-1 drugs like semaglutide. GIP receptor activation improves fat metabolism and may reduce the nausea burden that limits GLP-1-only treatment. GLP-1 receptor activation suppresses appetite, slows gastric emptying, and boosts insulin secretion. Those two pathways working together produce weight loss and glycemic control that neither achieves alone. SURMOUNT-1 (n=2,539) [1] showed dose-dependent results at 72 weeks. Its treatment-regimen estimand counts everyone randomized, including people who stopped the drug. On that basis, mean weight loss was 15.0% at 5 mg, 19.5% at 10 mg, and 20.9% at 15 mg, versus 3.1% on placebo. SURMOUNT-5 (n=751) [2] ran a direct comparison; tirzepatide reached 20.2% versus semaglutide's 13.7%. Roughly one in five tirzepatide patients lost 30% or more of their body weight. The r/Zepbound community (180,000+ members) confirms what the trials found. Appetite suppression starts within days. Most users stabilize at 7.5 to 12.5 mg rather than pushing to the maximum 15 mg dose. Cost and insurance coverage remain the biggest barriers. Weight regain after stopping is well-documented; about two-thirds of lost weight returns within a year of discontinuation.

Tirzepatide binds to two separate incretin receptors on the same molecule. At the GIP receptor, its affinity matches native GIP closely. At the GLP-1 receptor, affinity is roughly 18 to 20-fold lower, making it what researchers call an "imbalanced" agonist that leans toward GIP-mediated pathways. GLP-1 receptor activation does the heavy lifting on appetite. GLP-1 activation suppresses hunger signaling in the hypothalamus, slows gastric emptying so food stays in the stomach longer, and triggers glucose-dependent insulin release from pancreatic beta cells. These effects explain the "food noise" silencing that users describe within days of their first injection. GIP receptor activation adds a second layer. GIP activation improves insulin sensitivity, increases adiponectin (a fat-tissue hormone linked to metabolic health), and appears to improve beta-cell function over time. The GIP component may also explain why tirzepatide causes less nausea than pure GLP-1 agonists; SURMOUNT-5 recorded a GI discontinuation rate of just 2.7% for tirzepatide versus 5.6% for semaglutide. The combined effect on body weight exceeds what either pathway produces alone. SURMOUNT-1 data confirmed dose-dependent fat mass reduction, with approximately 75% of total weight loss coming from fat tissue and 25% from lean mass.
Tirzepatide benefits span weight loss, glycemic control, cardiovascular risk reduction, and metabolic improvement across multiple organ systems.

Tirzepatide achieved 20.9% mean weight loss at the 15 mg dose over 72 weeks in SURMOUNT-1, counting everyone randomized (n=2,539) [1]. Nearly one in three patients on the highest dose lost 25% or more.

Head-to-head superiority over semaglutide confirmed. SURMOUNT-5 (n=751) [2] showed 20.2% loss with tirzepatide versus 13.7% with semaglutide 2.4 mg at 72 weeks, with a lower GI dropout rate (2.7% vs 5.6%).
A1c reduction of 1.9 to 2.3 percentage points at 40 weeks in the SURPASS-1 and SURPASS-2 trials [3] [4]. That puts tirzepatide among the most potent glycemic agents available for type 2 diabetes.
SURMOUNT-OSA [5] showed a 55-63% reduction in apnea-hypopnea index scores. FDA approved tirzepatide for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea with obesity in December 2024.
Three-year T2D prevention data from the SURMOUNT-1 follow-up [6]: 94% of prediabetic participants on tirzepatide avoided progression to type 2 diabetes, compared to 40% with lifestyle changes alone.

SUMMIT trial [7] showed improvement in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) symptoms. SYNERGY-NASH [8] demonstrated MASH resolution in a high proportion of patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis.
Aligned
Scientific Evidence
Based on 22 key studies · FDA-approved
FDA-approved dual GIP/GLP-1 agonist with the strongest weight-loss efficacy of any approved drug class.
Dosing studied: 2.5 mg to 15 mg weekly (subcutaneous). Titrate by 2.5 mg increments every 4 weeks minimum.

SURMOUNT-1 demonstrated 20.9% mean body weight reduction at 15 mg over 72 weeks counting everyone randomized, and 22.5% among those who stayed on treatment. SURMOUNT-5 proved superiority over semaglutide 2.4 mg (−20.2% vs −13.7%). SURPASS-CVOT showed non-inferiority (not superiority) to dulaglutide for major cardiovascular events. Additional FDA approvals: obstructive sleep apnea (Dec 2024). SUMMIT (HFpEF) and SYNERGY-NASH (MASH) trials positive.
Key Study

SURMOUNT-1 (NEJM 2022, PMID 35658024): n=2,539 adults with obesity (no T2D), 72 weeks; −15.0% (5mg), −19.5% (10mg), −20.9% (15mg) vs −3.1% placebo, counting everyone randomized; −16.0%, −21.4%, −22.5% vs −2.4% among those who stayed on treatment. SURMOUNT-5 (NEJM 2025, PMID 40353578): n=751, open-label head-to-head, −20.2% tirzepatide vs −13.7% semaglutide 2.4mg at 72 weeks; 19.7% of tirzepatide patients lost ≥30% body weight vs 6.9% semaglutide. GI discontinuation rate lower with tirzepatide (2.7% vs 5.6%).
Limitations

Weight is largely regained after discontinuation: ~two-thirds within 12 months (SURMOUNT extension). Long-term human data beyond 72 weeks is limited outside of the 3-year T2D prevention endpoint. Black box warning for thyroid C-cell tumors remains: human relevance unknown. Approximately 25% of lost weight is lean mass without active resistance training. SURPASS-CVOT met non-inferiority vs dulaglutide but did not meet superiority on primary MACE endpoint (HR 0.92, 95.3% CI 0.83 to 1.01). No head-to-head cardiovascular outcomes data vs semaglutide.
Community Experience
Strongest community enthusiasm of any GLP-1. r/Zepbound users consistently report superior appetite suppression and weight loss vs their prior semaglutide experience.
Community dosing: 2.5 mg to 15 mg weekly. Majority stabilize at 7.5–12.5 mg. Many intentionally stay at their lowest effective dose rather than escalating to maximum.

Primary concerns: cost and insurance denials, GI side effects during escalation, muscle loss, and fear of lifelong dependency. Slow titration (6-8 weeks per step vs FDA's 4 weeks) is the dominant community protocol for GI tolerance.

Science & Community Aligned

Science and community fully agree on core findings: tirzepatide produces 20%+ weight loss at maximum tolerated doses, GI side effects are the limiting factor during titration, and weight returns when stopped. Community-evolved slow titration (6-8 week steps) is evidence-consistent and not in label. Community preference to stay at lowest effective dose (not always escalating to 15mg) aligns with clinical guidance that the right dose is the lowest achieving therapeutic goals.

Tirzepatide comes in pre-filled pens (brand Zepbound/Mounjaro) and compounded vials (very limited availability since March 2025). For compounded vials: Reconstitution math for a 10 mg vial with 2 mL bacteriostatic water gives you 5 mg/mL. A 2.5 mg dose is 0.5 mL (50 units on an insulin syringe). A 5 mg dose is 1.0 mL (100 units, a full syringe). For a 15 mg vial with 2 mL BAC water, concentration is 7.5 mg/mL. A 7.5 mg dose is 1.0 mL (100 units). A 10 mg dose runs about 1.33 mL, which exceeds a standard 1 mL syringe; either use a 3 mL syringe or reconstitute with 3 mL instead (giving 5 mg/mL, then 2.0 mL per 10 mg dose). The thing most beginners miss: 2.5 mg is not a therapeutic dose for weight loss. It's a tolerability test. Don't judge whether tirzepatide "works" until you've been at 5 mg for at least 4 weeks. Evening injections help most people sleep through the nausea window (4 to 8 hours post-dose).
Cycling Protocol
Intended for long-term use. Weight regain expected upon discontinuation. Maintenance dosing may be lower than escalation dose.
Tirzepatide Cycle

Tirzepatide is an FDA-approved medication intended for continuous long-term use, not cycled like research peptides. Weight regain begins within weeks of discontinuation and most patients regain approximately two-thirds of lost weight within 12 months of stopping (SURMOUNT-1 extension data). Its listed cycle (52 weeks on, no scheduled off period) reflects this: indefinite continuous use is standard practice. Any dose reductions should be gradual and medically supervised. The clinical question is not "when to cycle off" but "what is the lowest effective maintenance dose."
Dose reduction appropriate only if target weight maintained for 12+ months at therapeutic dose: attempt cautious step-down under medical supervision
Discontinuation required for pregnancy (stop ≥2 months before planned conception)
Discontinuation required for confirmed MTC, MEN2 diagnosis, anaphylaxis, or severe pancreatitis
Medication holidays are not an established practice: weight regain risk is high within weeks of stopping
Gather supplies: tirzepatide vial (or pre-filled pen), bacteriostatic water (if reconstituting a vial), alcohol swabs, insulin syringe (31-32 gauge, 4-6 mm needle for subcutaneous injection).

If using a compounded vial: add 2 mL bacteriostatic water slowly down the side of the vial. Swirl gently until dissolved. Never shake. For a 10 mg vial, final concentration is 5 mg/mL. For a 15 mg vial, concentration is 7.5 mg/mL.

Draw your dose At 5 mg/mL concentration: 50 units on the syringe equals 2.5 mg. 100 units equals 5 mg. At 7.5 mg/mL concentration: 100 units equals 7.5 mg. 67 units equals approximately 5 mg. Calculate your dose carefully for each vial concentration.
Clean the injection site with an alcohol swab Choose abdomen (2 inches from the navel), thigh (front or outer), or upper arm. Rotate sites each week.
Pinch the skin gently and insert the needle at a 90-degree angle. Inject slowly and hold for 5 to 10 seconds before withdrawing.

Inject once weekly, same day each week Many users prefer evening injections to sleep through the 4 to 8 hour nausea window. Timing relative to meals isn't critical, but small, low-fat meals for 24 to 48 hours after injection improve tolerability.

Titration schedule: start at 2.5 mg for at least 4 weeks Increase by 2.5 mg every 4 weeks (or 6 to 8 weeks per the community protocol if GI symptoms persist). Target your lowest effective dose; not everyone needs 15 mg.

Storage: refrigerate reconstituted vials at 2-8 degrees C (36-46 degrees F). Use within 4 weeks. Brand pens follow the same storage requirements. Pre-filled pens can be stored at room temperature (up to 30 degrees C / 86 degrees F) for up to 21 days per the Zepbound label.

Community-used adjunct for GI side effects of tirzepatide. BPC-157 supports gastric mucosal healing and may reduce nausea and GI inflammation during dose escalation. No clinical trial data exists for this combination.

Anti-inflammatory tripeptide used by community members with co-occurring IBS or IBD and obesity. Hypothesized to complement gut health during GI-heavy tirzepatide side effect phases. No clinical data.
500 mcg oral daily, concurrent with tirzepatide use.

Community stack for energy support and mitochondrial function during caloric deficit and rapid weight loss. No known interaction with tirzepatide. No clinical data for this combination.
Avoid
Semaglutide

Both activate GLP-1 receptors: combining produces additive GLP-1 stimulation with dramatically increased nausea, vomiting, dehydration, and hypoglycemia risk. No additive benefit over tirzepatide monotherapy. When switching from semaglutide to tirzepatide, allow at least one half-life (~7 days) before starting tirzepatide to avoid overlap.
Liraglutide
GLP-1 receptor agonist: overlapping mechanism with tirzepatide's GLP-1 component. Combination increases GI side effects and hypoglycemia risk with no additive weight-loss benefit.
Retatrutide
Triple agonist (GIP/GLP-1/GCG) with fully overlapping GIP and GLP-1 receptor targets. Combining is mechanistically redundant and dramatically increases GI side effects and hypoglycemia risk.
MK-677 (Ibutamoren)

GH secretagogue that significantly stimulates appetite via the ghrelin pathway: directly antagonizes tirzepatide's primary appetite-suppression mechanism. Also promotes insulin resistance, opposing tirzepatide's glycemic benefits.

Tirzepatide carries a black box warning for thyroid C-cell tumors. In rodent studies, it caused dose-dependent increases in thyroid C-cell tumors, including medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC). Whether this translates to humans is unknown, and no confirmed human cases have been attributed to tirzepatide. The drug is contraindicated in anyone with a personal or family history of MTC or Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN2). Gastrointestinal side effects are the most common reason people struggle with tirzepatide. In the SURMOUNT and SURPASS trials, nausea affected 12 to 29% of patients (dose-dependent, worst at higher weight-management doses). Diarrhea occurred in 13 to 17%. Vomiting hit 8 to 10%. Constipation affected 7 to 11%. Most of these effects are mild-to-moderate and improve with slow dose titration; the community-preferred 6 to 8 week steps between dose increases reduce GI burden compared to the FDA label's 4-week minimum. Decreased appetite (9 to 11%) is technically a side effect, though most users consider it the primary benefit. Sulfur burps are a community-reported nuisance during escalation phases that clinical trials don't track well. Hair thinning (telogen effluvium) affects roughly 4 to 5% of users versus about 1% on placebo. This isn't a direct drug effect. Rapid weight loss and caloric restriction trigger a hair growth cycle shift that typically starts 2 to 3 months in and resolves on its own by month 9 to 12. Injection-site reactions occur in 4 to 7% of patients. Rotating injection sites between the abdomen, thigh, and upper arm helps. Let the vial reach room temperature for 15 to 20 minutes before injecting. Pancreatitis is rare but serious. Severe, persistent abdominal pain warrants immediate medical evaluation. Serum lipase testing should happen only when pancreatitis is clinically suspected; routine screening isn't indicated. Gallbladder disease and hypersensitivity reactions are uncommon but documented in clinical trials. Stop tirzepatide and seek medical care if you develop signs of anaphylaxis, severe abdominal pain, or jaundice. Low blood pressure is a smaller but real signal. On the Zepbound label, hypotension hit 1.6% on tirzepatide vs 0.1% on placebo in the pooled weight-loss trials. It ran higher in people also taking blood pressure medication (2.2% vs 1.2% without it) and showed up alongside gastrointestinal side effects and dehydration. A 2026 meta-analysis pooled 32 randomized trials of tirzepatide and semaglutide (47,332 people) [9]. Tirzepatide carried 2.45 times the risk of hypotension-related events (95% CI 1.35 to 4.45). The risk rose at higher doses, and semaglutide showed no significant change. Lightheadedness when you stand up is worth a blood pressure check, especially if you take antihypertensives. Muscle loss is a legitimate concern. Approximately 25% of weight lost on tirzepatide is lean mass (SURMOUNT-1 body composition data). Resistance training 3 to 4 times per week and protein intake of at least 1.2 g/kg body weight per day are the primary countermeasures. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: tirzepatide is contraindicated. Stop treatment at least 2 months before planned conception due to the 5-day half-life and limited reproductive safety data.
Common Issues & Solutions

Nausea after injection: Take injection in the evening to sleep through peak plasma levels (4-8 hr post-dose). Eat small, low-fat meals for 24-48 hr post-injection. If nausea is severe, hold at current dose for 6-8 weeks before attempting escalation. Ginger tea, B6, or ondansetron (if prescribed) are community-used adjuncts.

Weight-loss plateau: First verify protein intake (≥1.2 g/kg), caloric balance, and that food habits have not crept back. A 4-8 week plateau at a stable dose is normal during recomposition. If confirmed plateau after 8+ weeks, escalate dose by one 2.5 mg step. Adding resistance training accelerates fat loss during plateaus.

Constipation: Daily fiber target 25-35g. Add psyllium husk (1-2 tbsp/day) or polyethylene glycol (MiraLAX): most effective OTC option in this context. Minimum 2L water daily. Physical activity stimulates GI motility. Do not use stimulant laxatives long-term.

Hair thinning (telogen effluvium): Typically starts 2-3 months into significant weight loss, peaks at 3-6 months, self-resolves by month 9-12. Not a direct tirzepatide effect: consequence of caloric restriction and physiological stress. Ensure adequate protein, iron, zinc, and biotin intake.

Injection site reactions: Rotate sites systematically between abdomen, thigh, and upper arm. Allow peptide to warm to room temperature (15-20 min out of fridge) before injecting. Use 4-6 mm, 31-32 gauge needle for SC injection. Avoid areas of lipohypertrophy. Lumps/bruising are normal but avoid the same site for 1-2 weeks.

Tirzepatide is FDA-approved under two brand names: Mounjaro (type 2 diabetes, approved May 2022) and Zepbound (chronic weight management, approved November 2023). A third indication for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea with obesity was approved in December 2024. In December 2025, FDA extended Mounjaro's type 2 diabetes indication to pediatric patients 10 years and older. In August 2026, based on SURPASS-CVOT, FDA added a cardiovascular indication. Its label now adds reducing the risk of cardiovascular death, non-fatal heart attack or non-fatal stroke in high-risk adults with type 2 diabetes. Tirzepatide requires a prescription in the United States and most countries. Compounded tirzepatide availability changed significantly in 2025. The FDA ended enforcement discretion for 503B outsourcing facilities on March 19, 2025, and for 503A pharmacies on February 18, 2025. A federal court upheld this decision in May 2025. Tirzepatide is not on the FDA drug shortage list. FDA said so in a May 1, 2026 Federal Register notice (2026-08552), and FDA's shortage data still listed no tirzepatide shortage in October 2026. LillyDirect sells brand Zepbound vials and KwikPens (not compounded) to self-pay patients. Its October 2026 prices start at $299 a month for 2.5 mg and $399 for 5 mg. Doses of 7.5 to 15 mg cost $449 a month when you refill within 45 days, or $499 to $699 if you don't. Tirzepatide is not on WADA's 2026 Prohibited List. WADA's 2026 Monitoring Program tracks markers of semaglutide and tirzepatide in and out of competition. Monitoring watches for misuse without banning the drug. This content is for informational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice. Consult a licensed healthcare provider before starting any medication.

phases.syringeUnits: 100 units (15 mg vial + 2 mL BAC water → 7.5 mg/mL; 1.0 mL per dose)
phases.notes: FDA maintenance dose option. Many patients achieve adequate weight loss here and stop escalating.

phases.name: Phase 4: Maintenance Option B
phases.syringeUnits: 67 units (15 mg vial + 2 mL BAC water → 7.5 mg/mL; ~0.67 mL per dose)
phases.notes: FDA maintenance dose option. SURMOUNT-1: −19.5% mean weight loss at 72 weeks at this dose.

phases.name: Phase 5: Maintenance Option C
phases.notes: FDA maintenance dose option. SURMOUNT-1 tested 5, 10 and 15 mg, not 12.5 mg. Incremental benefit over 10mg is modest; many stay at 10mg.

phases.name: Phase 6: Maximum Dose
phases.notes: FDA maximum approved dose. SURMOUNT-1: −20.9% mean weight loss at 72 weeks. SURMOUNT-5: −20.2% at maximum tolerated dose (10mg or 15mg). Intended as long-term maintenance; weight regain expected on discontinuation.

protocols.duration: 72 weeks minimum based on pivotal trials; intended for long-term/indefinite use per FDA label
protocols.monitoringNotes: A1c and fasting glucose at baseline and 3-month intervals (T2D). Renal function if significant GI fluid losses. TSH if symptoms of thyroid disease. Serum lipase only if severe abdominal pain (not routine screen). Lipid panel and blood pressure at 6-month intervals. Weight and waist circumference monthly.

protocols.goal: Weight loss: slow titration for GI-sensitive users

phases.name: Extended Start
phases.syringeUnits: 50 units (10 mg vial + 2 mL BAC water → 5 mg/mL)
phases.notes: Community consensus: extend to 6 weeks if any GI symptoms present. Do not rush escalation.

phases.name: Step 2
phases.notes: Hold 6-8 weeks. Drop back to 2.5mg for 2 weeks if GI side effects are severe, then re-attempt 5mg.

phases.name: Extended Maintenance
phases.notes: Community recommendation: stay at lowest dose that silences food noise and produces measurable weight loss. No requirement to reach 15mg. Most community members plateau between 7.5-12.5mg.

protocols.duration: Indefinite; most community users treat as long-term lifestyle medication
protocols.monitoringNotes: Protein intake ≥1.2 g/kg/day: community standard. Track lean mass if access to DEXA or InBody. Daily fiber intake (25-35g) to offset constipation. Scale weight weekly but assess trend over 4-week blocks, not day-to-day.

protocols.goal: Weight loss with lean mass preservation (concurrent resistance training)

phases.name: Titration + Training Foundation
phases.notes: Begin resistance training at week 2 or as soon as energy allows. Target 3-4 sessions/week of compound lifts. Protein target: 1.6–2.0 g/kg body weight. Systematic review (PMC12394919, 2025) supports resistance training as primary lean mass preservation strategy.

phases.name: Maintenance + Recomposition
phases.notes: Continue resistance training. SURMOUNT-1 compositional data: ~75% of total weight loss is fat mass, ~25% lean mass. Resistance training and adequate protein can shift this ratio favorably. DEXA scan at baseline and every 6 months recommended.

protocols.duration: Indefinite with structured periodization of resistance training
protocols.monitoringNotes: DEXA or InBody scan every 6 months. Creatinine and BMP for renal function. Strength markers (squat/deadlift/press 1RM) to confirm lean mass maintenance. Protein intake log.

faqs.q: What is the recommended tirzepatide dosage?
faqs.a: Start at 2.5 mg weekly for 4 weeks, then titrate to 5 mg. From there, increases of 2.5 mg every 4 weeks up to a maximum of 15 mg weekly. SURMOUNT-1 used the 5/10/15 mg doses. Most weight loss benefit hits a ceiling around 10-15 mg for most people.

faqs.q: What are the side effects of tirzepatide?
faqs.a: Nausea (17-25%, dose-dependent), diarrhea (13-17%), and vomiting (8-10%) were the most common in SURMOUNT-1. These peak during dose escalation and usually resolve within 4-8 weeks at a stable dose. Injection site reactions occur in about 3-7%. Pancreatitis, gallbladder events, and gastroparesis are rare but documented.

faqs.q: How does tirzepatide compare to semaglutide?
faqs.a: Tirzepatide targets both GIP and GLP-1 receptors; semaglutide targets GLP-1 only. SURMOUNT-1 showed 20.9% mean weight loss at 72 weeks on 15 mg tirzepatide. Semaglutide's STEP 1 showed 14.9% at 68 weeks on 2.4 mg. SURMOUNT-5 (PMID 40353578, n=751) ran a direct comparison: tirzepatide 15 mg achieved 20.2% weight loss versus 13.7% for semaglutide 2.4 mg at 72 weeks.

Yes. Mounjaro is FDA-approved for type 2 diabetes (2022) and Zepbound for chronic weight management (2023). Both are manufactured by Eli Lilly. The weight management approval covers adults with BMI 30+ or BMI 27+ with a weight-related comorbidity.

faqs.q: How long does tirzepatide take to work?
faqs.a: Most users notice appetite reduction within the first 1-2 weeks. Measurable weight loss typically appears by week 4-8. The SURMOUNT-1 trial showed the steepest weight loss curve between weeks 12-36, with results plateauing around week 60-72.

Tirzepatide earns an A on the Peptide Schedule safety scale as an FDA-approved dual agonist, though it carries a black box warning for thyroid C-cell tumors seen in rodents, with human relevance unknown. Gastrointestinal effects are the main limiter, with nausea in 12 to 29% of trial participants, worst at higher weight-management doses, though the GI discontinuation rate was lower than semaglutide in SURMOUNT-5 (2.7% vs 5.6%). A personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2 is a contraindication.
Tirzepatide typically comes in 5mg or 10mg or 15mg vials. Add 2mL of bacteriostatic water to the vial. Use the free calculator for exact syringe units based on your desired dose.

faqs.q: What is the half-life of Tirzepatide?
faqs.a: The half-life of Tirzepatide is ~5 days. This determines how frequently you need to dose for consistent blood levels.

summary: 20.9% mean body weight reduction at 72 weeks on the 15 mg dose, counting everyone randomized. Tirzepatide (Mounjaro, Zepbound, CAS 2023788-19-2) is an FDA-approved dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist, the first drug in its class to target both incretin hormones at once.

notes.text: On the FDA label, the only contraindications are a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2, and a prior serious hypersensitivity reaction. Pancreatitis history, severe GI disease (e.g. gastroparesis) and pregnancy are warnings or precautions there, not formal contraindications. The label's missed-dose rule: take it within 4 days, otherwise skip it and dose on your usual day.
